reason: Once the source was found, the first reading was reread against it on the images. This corrected misreadings (e.g. 'Nemo' for 'R(ati)o', 'felicitas', 'beatificantur') and showed that the catalogued r/v faces are reversed.
sources: Jacobus de Voragine, Sermones quadragesimales, Venice 1582, Internet Archive bub_gb_O3KLJ6rfkL4C, page images n137, n200 (fol. 92r), n223 (fol. 104r), n225, n282, n288, n443-445
Jacobus de Voragine, Sermones quadragesimales, Venice 1528 (Google Books D_8oTUKduSIC), snippet for 'compassibilis'
Gerard de Frachet, Vitae fratrum ordinis praedicatorum, ed. B. M. Reichert (MOPH 1, 1896), I.4, pp. v and 33, Google Books snippet text
text:
Source-assisted reading of F-ssa8 (Stams, Frg. 47). These lines were reread on the native images with the Venice 1582 edition of Voragine's Sermones quadragesimales at hand. One research reader reread 47_7r col. a, 47_5v (lines 1-18), 47_8r col. b, 47_15v col. a and the 47_1r prayer block. A second research reader read 47_10r col. a, 47_14r col. b, the lower block of 47_4r and the top of 47_15r col. a blind, before opening the source, and corrected them against it. All other faces rest on the image-only first reading. Boxes are x,y,width,height in native pixels (images 4912 x 7360). (x) marks an expansion, [ ] lost or supplied text, ? a doubtful reading. On 47_4, 47_5, 47_8 and 47_15 the face catalogued "v" is the original recto.
